P2118.overview: The ECM monitors throttle-actuator motor current. A resistance/performance fault trips P2118 when the measured current falls outside the modelled range for the commanded throttle position.

cause.winding: Open or high-resistance throttle motor winding
cause.wiring: Damaged motor supply or ground wiring

P2118.repair: Replace the throttle body assembly (integrated actuator motor). Clear codes, perform throttle-actuator adaptation, and confirm TP1/TP2 correlation and current return to spec.

scenario.title: Intermittent power loss under load
scenario.desc: A 2019 Camry arrives with a complaint of power loss on inclines and an illuminated MIL. Two fault codes are present in the ECM and they are not equally relevant. Work the process in order and justify each conclusion with a measurement — the simulator scores your route, not just your answer.

obj.0: Separate a symptom-relevant code from a consequential one.
obj.1: Use set-point versus actual comparison instead of absolute values.
obj.2: Test load dependency before condemning a component.
obj.3: Work upstream from the failure point to the supply side.

report.customerComplaint: Loss of power under load on inclines, occasional rough idle when warm, MIL illuminated. Fault reported as intermittent over the past three weeks.

assist.seed: You have P0087 and P2118 in the ECM. Before I say anything about parts: what is the actual rail pressure against the requested value at idle?
assist.t0b: I have not measured it yet
assist.r0: Rail pressure is 46 bar short of the set-point at idle. A control fault and a supply restriction look identical from here. Snap the throttle to 3 000 rpm — does the gap widen or hold constant?
assist.t1a: The gap widens to about 120 bar
assist.r1: A gap that grows with demand is a volume problem, not a control problem. Next, move to the low-pressure side: what is the feed pressure before the high-pressure pump?
assist.r2: 2.1 bar against a 4.5 – 5.5 bar specification starves the high-pressure pump, so it can never reach the requested rail pressure. Confirm the filter restriction and pump delivery volume before condemning anything on the high-pressure side.
assist.t3b: Show me the wiring for the low-pressure pump
assist.r3: Your reasoning chain is sound: symptom → set-point deviation → load dependency → upstream supply. Log the delivery-volume test in the report so the next technician can see why the high-pressure pump was not replaced.

none.label: Healthy
none.desc: No fault injected. The capture should sit inside the manual values.

open.label: Open circuit
open.desc: Circuit broken between the component and the ECU. The driver never pulls the line down.

shortGnd.label: Short to ground
shortGnd.desc: The measured line is shorted to chassis ground — it can no longer rise.

shortBat.label: Short to battery
shortBat.desc: The measured line is shorted to a supply — it can no longer be pulled down.

highRes.label: High resistance
highRes.desc: Corrosion or a poor crimp adds resistance; amplitude collapses and edges soften.

weak.label: Weak sensor
weak.desc: Component output has degraded with wear. Shape is correct, amplitude is not.

noise.label: Noise
noise.desc: Unscreened wiring or a failing ground injects interference on top of the signal.

poorGnd.label: Poor ground
poorGnd.desc: Sensor ground is offset above chassis; the whole trace is lifted and unstable.

dropout.label: Dropout
dropout.desc: The signal disappears for whole cycles then returns.

intermittent.label: Intermittent
intermittent.desc: Fault appears in bursts — only visible on a long capture.

missing.label: Missing pulses
missing.desc: Pulses are missing from the pattern; the ECU loses synchronisation.

coilWeak.label: Damaged coil
coilWeak.desc: Primary inductive kick is far below spec — weak spark, secondary breakdown.

injShort.label: Injector winding
injShort.desc: Partially shorted injector winding: current rises too fast and too high.

ai.supply: Ch A is on a supply terminal — a flat line at supply voltage means the probe is on the feed, not the signal. Move Ch A to the signal terminal.
ai.ground: Ch A is on a ground terminal — the trace sits on 0 V with only noise. Nothing is being measured.
ai.none: No signal probe connected — the trace is only noise. Connect Ch A to the signal terminal and the ground clip.
ai.spec: Signal matches the reference for this component — shape, amplitude and timing all sit inside the manual values. Record it as a known-good reference.

inj.instruction: Ch A on the injector driver terminal, ground clip to battery negative, current clamp around the supply wire. Trigger falling on Ch A, then read the spike height and the pulse width between cursors.
inj.function: The ECU switches the injector low side to ground. Current builds through the winding, the pintle lifts, and on switch-off the collapsing field produces the inductive voltage spike. Spike height and pulse width tell you winding condition and fuelling.
bullets: Solenoid winding with a spring-loaded pintle
Low-side switched by the ECU driver
Peak & hold drivers current-limit after opening
Spike height depends on winding inductance
probeNotes: Back-probe terminal 2; do not pierce the insulation.
Ground clip on the battery negative post, not on a painted bracket.
Clamp the supply wire only — both wires in the clamp cancel out.

coil.instruction: Ch A on the switched primary terminal, clamp on the +B feed. Watch current limiting during dwell, then the inductive kick and burn line at switch-off.
coil.function: The module switches the primary winding to ground; the magnetic field builds until the current limit, then collapses to induce the secondary high voltage. Primary voltage shows dwell, current limiting and the inductive kick.
bullets: Primary electromagnet and high-voltage secondary winding
Current-limited module with a low-resistance coil
One coil per cylinder, individually driven
Kick height falls when the winding or the ground degrades
probeNotes: Use an attenuator or a ×10 probe: primary kick exceeds 300 V.
Clamp the +B wire to see the current limit plateau.
Never disconnect a coil with the engine running.

cam.instruction: Ch A on the signal terminal, ground clip on the sensor ground. Confirm both levels, then count the segment pattern over one camshaft revolution.
cam.function: A semiconductor converts the changing magnetic field of the rotor into a switched voltage. Because it is a Hall device, amplitude does not change with engine speed — only the pattern timing does.
bullets: Hall element with internal amplifier and output stage
Output level set by the supply voltage, not by rpm
Rotor segments give an asymmetric pattern for cylinder ID
MRE variants behave identically on the scope
probeNotes: Measure with the connector attached — an unloaded Hall output reads wrong.
Ground on terminal 3, the sensor ground, to see the true low level.
A clean square wave with a wrong pattern still means a mechanical timing fault.

app.instruction: Ch A on VPA, Ch B on VPA2, ground on EPA. Sweep the pedal slowly full travel and back; both traces must move together with no steps or dropouts.
app.function: Two independent voltage dividers move with the pedal angle. The ECU compares both signals for plausibility, so the ratio between the tracks matters as much as the values.
bullets: Sliding contacts on two resistive tracks
Separate supplies and resistances per track
Independent signals for malfunction detection
Wear shows as spikes or flat spots mid-travel
probeNotes: Both tracks referenced to their own ground — do not share EPA and EPA2.
Sweep slowly: a worn track shows as a narrow spike, easy to miss fast.
Compare the ratio, not just the endpoints.

map.instruction: Ch A on PIM, ground on E2. Capture a snap-throttle event: the trace must follow load without steps, and settle back to the idle value.
map.function: A silicone diaphragm with integral strain gauges compares manifold pressure to a sealed reference vacuum. The resistance change is converted to a voltage proportional to engine load.
bullets: Silicone diaphragm with four strain gauges
Sealed reference vacuum on one side
5 V supply from a regulator in the ECU
A digital variant outputs frequency instead of voltage
probeNotes: Check the 5 V supply on terminal 1 before condemning the sensor.
Ground on E2 at the sensor, so a poor sensor ground shows up.
A hose leak looks like a lazy sensor — check the vacuum line first.

knock.instruction: Ch A on the signal terminal, ground on the shield. AC coupling only. Tap near the sensor with a small hammer and compare burst amplitude with background noise.
knock.function: A piezoelectric crystal between the body and a seismic mass produces a voltage proportional to the changing force. The ECU amplifies and filters the signal to isolate detonation frequencies.
bullets: Piezo crystal compressed by a seismic mass
Signal amplified and band-filtered inside the ECU
Screened cable — shield integrity is critical
Infinite resistance when measured cold and disconnected
probeNotes: AC coupling: the DC offset hides the burst.
Keep the probe lead away from ignition leads — it picks up the coil.
A loose mounting bolt reads exactly like a weak sensor.

lambda.instruction: Ch A on the signal terminal, ground on the sensor ground. Warm the engine, then count crossings per second and check both extremes are reached.
lambda.function: The zirconia ceramic compares exhaust oxygen with reference air and generates its own voltage. The ECU uses the switching rate and the extremes to trim the mixture and to judge the catalyst.
bullets: Zirconium dioxide ceramic with electrodes on both faces
Integrated heater reaches operating temperature quickly
Never measure resistance on a zirconia sensor
Response time increases as the sensor wears
probeNotes: Never use an ohmmeter on a zirconia sensor.
The sensor generates its own voltage — no supply to check on the signal wire.
A lazy switch rate matters more than the peak values.
